findings.title: Brittle SynchronizationContext installation in non-WinForms STA host
findings.evidence: If no `SynchronizationContext` is installed on that thread, the add-in installs a `WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext` ... before capturing
findings.problem: SolidWorks own message pump and potential co-existing add-ins expect native STA behavior; injecting WinForms context can alter modal dialog handling, COM event delivery ordering, or introduce hidden message filters that only surface under load or specific UI actions (e.g. property manager pages).
findings.why_it_matters: The entire threading model, reentrancy rule, and cancellation semantics rest on this assumption; opposite assumption (SW thread already owns its context) makes the install path a latent source of deadlocks or lost messages not exercised by StaCommandQueueTests.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture existing context without replacement; provide custom SynchronizationContext subclass that only posts to SW's known window handle message queue, removing WinForms dependency.

findings.title: ToolCallRegistry state machine survives only in-memory process lifetime
findings.evidence: `ToolCallRegistry` is session-scoped ... survives WebSocket reconnects within the same session and is cleared only on session reset (new `AddinSessionId`). On SolidWorks restart, the add-in re-runs `ConnectToSW` and a new `AddinSessionId` is generated.
findings.problem: If SolidWorks crashes or is force-terminated, all in-flight Abandoned/Completed state disappears; orchestrator reconnect receives fresh AddinSessionId yet may replay CallIds that the new process treats as new, violating the "client knows to use a new CallId" contract and leaving model in inconsistent state without detection.
findings.why_it_matters: Assumes perfect process lifetime and no external termination — exactly the unplanned-disconnect scenario the spec tries to harden against; creates adversarial condition where viewer cannot distinguish crash-induced partial state from intentional changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist minimal registry (CallId → terminal state + final StateVersion) to registry or shared JSON under AddinSessionId; load on ConnectToSW and reconcile with orchestrator on handshake.

findings.title: Complexity inflation in five-state deduplication registry vs simpler SPEC-03 contract
findings.evidence: Tracker holds one of five states: `Queued`, `Executing`, `Completed`, `Cancelled`, or `Abandoned` ... 60-second retention window ... `IN_FLIGHT_DUPLICATE`, `EXPIRED_CALL_ID`, `TERMINATED_CALL_ID`
findings.problem: Introduces combinatorial test matrix (InFlightDeduplicationTests, DisconnectExecutingCommandTests, DisconnectRollbackTests) and multiple error codes that SPEC-03 must now special-case, while the underlying COM non-preemptibility is already documented in 2.4.
findings.why_it_matters: If the opposite assumption holds — that unique CallIds and higher-level lifecycle timeouts suffice — the entire registry, cache expiry, and abandonment tracking become unnecessary scaffolding likely to cause downstream rework when SPEC-03 integrates.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove registry retention and state machine; let ToolDispatcher return `Cancelled` or normal result; require SPEC-03 to enforce unique CallIds and handle timeouts without adapter-level replay.

findings.title: Screenshot directory convention creates brittle cross-process dependency without hardening
findings.evidence: If the `BSVOICE_SCREENSHOT_DIR` environment variable is set, its value is used instead ... orchestrator validates that this path is readable from its process context by creating and deleting a temporary file. If validation fails, the orchestrator logs a warning and disables screenshot-dependent features
findings.problem: Assumes orchestrator and add-in share exact same user context and permissions forever; no handling for ACL mismatches, network share latency, antivirus locking, or path-length limits on generated `{utcTicks}_{callId}.png` under rapid tool calls.
findings.why_it_matters: Turns a supposedly transparent file convention into a single point of failure that can silently degrade functionality mid-session; adversarial scenario of orchestrator running under different elevation or containerized breaks the "no negotiation needed" claim.
findings.proposed_fix: Require both processes to use identical environment-variable contract with mandatory validation at handshake; add fallback in-memory base64 transmission for critical screenshots when directory validation fails.

findings.title: Omission of SolidWorks multi-instance and safe-mode edge cases
findings.evidence: SolidWorks target: 2025 SP3+ (COM API backward-compat holds to 2024 SP5 for most methods; Day-0 validation catches any regressions)
findings.problem: No mention of behavior when multiple SolidWorks instances run concurrently, when SW is started in safe mode (disables some COM events and templates), or when user has non-default registry hive; AddinSessionIdGenerator reads HKLM MachineGuid but falls back to per-user file without distinguishing SW instances.
findings.why_it_matters: The session identity, reconnect handshake, and event suppression logic implicitly assume a single global SolidWorks process; real-world engineering workstations frequently run parallel versions, exposing the design to state leakage across instances.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend AddinSessionId inputs with SW process command-line or HWND of main window; add safe-mode detection in Day-0 validation and explicit out-of-scope note if unsupported.
